# Generated by scripts/citation-lint.sh --write (#85). Two blocks.
#
# PINS: one line per distinct DESIGN.md citation form in the tree, beside the
# first words of the item it resolves to. A changed line means DESIGN.md
# renumbered or an item was reworded; read the diff before regenerating.
#
# EXTERNAL: citations in DESIGN.md's own notation that name a DIFFERENT
# document, declared per file and form -- with the number of sites each
# declaration covers, so it cannot silently grow -- and so exempted knowingly
# rather than guessed at. An undeclared unresolvable citation is an error.
#
# AUTHORITY. This baseline is AUDITED, not assumed. On 2026-08-16 every
# DESIGN-bound citation site was read at the meaning level -- cited ordinal
# against the content the citing site actually invokes -- because a pin
# certifies stability, never birth-correctness, and would freeze a
# wrong-from-birth ordinal with perfect fidelity. Census BEFORE the sweep:
#   120 sites; 8 naming another document; 112 DESIGN-bound, of which 92
#   land on the content the citing site invokes and 20 were mis-minted
#   (18 x '§5.4' + DESIGN.md:129 '§7 rule 6' + l1_test.go:26 '§5.2').
# The sweep rewrote 16 of the 20 to the explicit form and marked the other
# 4 citation-lint:quote -- they are deliberate quotations of the bad form,
# and normalizing them would erase the defect they document. Of the 92 that
# were already right, the 25 using the §X.Y shorthand were left byte-for-byte:
# rewriting a correct citation in the document the gates cite as grounds is
# churn dressed as rigour.
#
# The CURRENT tally is deliberately not recorded here. It changes every time
# anyone cites a rule, and a hardcoded copy of it would be a cache with no
# invalidation protocol -- the trap DESIGN.md §5 rule 8 names. The script
# prints it on every run; the census above is a dated historical fact about
# one audit and does not go stale.
# A pin failure therefore means a reference MOVED off an audited target. It
# does not re-establish that the target was ever right: that took reading,
# once, and a later sweep of this size needs reading again.
